newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia to release rabbit virus around Oct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia to release rabbit virus around Oct.

text.p: Australia will nationally release the rabbit calicivirus around October, Primary Industries Minister John Anderson told reporters on MOnday.
The decision followed agreement between federal and state governments to approve of the virus as a biological control agent, the minister said.
Rabbits, which are not native to Australia, cost the farm sector nearly A$600 million a year.

"They eat pastures, crops, forests, tree plantations, and native vegetation; they compete with livestock for food; they contribute to land degradation and soil erosion; and they reduce options for land managers to control grazing pressure and respond to drought," Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said.
A spokesman for the national Bureau of Resource Sciences, Peter O'Brien, said there would be 280 release sites nationally in all states and territories.
"Vials of the virus will be used to innoculate wild rabbits which will than be placed back into warrens and this will then spread from rabbit to rabbit," he told reporters.
The clean-up programme would cost the national and state governments a total A$100 million, Anderson said.
"As required, we'll work through those (cost) issues and the release will begin early next month," he said.

The virus was released accidentally last year, killing millions of rabbits as it spread throughout the outback of the state of South Australia. Australia has an estimated 500 million rabbits. -- Canberra bureau 61-6 273-2730
